title: In some countries family and friends who care for the elderly do not find time to look aft…
question: In some countries family and friends who care for the elderly do not find time to look after them. What are the reasons and solutions?
answer:
It is a sad reality that in some parts of the world, close friends and even family members are 
facing difficulty in finding time to look after the older members. There are many reasons for 
this situation and steps are needed to ensure that people in their later stages of life are taken 
care of and loved. 
 
Firstly, today most people have a busy and hectic schedule. Besides their caregiver duties, 
they also have to tend to their children, their jobs and other responsibilities. Secondly, the 
increasing life expectancy has meant that the working generations have to take care of the 
elderly for a longer time span than earlier. The longer life expectancy also means that in some 
families, young people have to take care of two old generations in place of one.  
 
There are many steps that can be taken to address this situation. To begin with, whenever 
possible, people can take the work from home option, so that they can spend some extra time 
with the elder members. If this is not possible, they can hire caregivers for certain hours. 
Caregivers not only help with health and exercise needs of the elderly but also keep the old 
people lively by providing them someone to talk to. 
 
In addition, the young members in the family can familiarize the elderly with technology, so 
that the elder members can stay connected with them, even when they are busy. Technology 
can also help reduce the dependence on the young. For example, if the old people have 
mobility issues, they can order things online instead of asking the young members to get them 
the items. Finally, the elderly need to be accommodating and must be willing to make certain 
changes, especially when it comes to their health. 
 
To sum up, there are various causes why the young generation is facing time issues to look 
after their elderly family members, but with certain steps they can alleviate these problems.

title: Caring for children is an important thing of the society. It is suggested that all mothers…
question: Caring for children is an important thing of the society. It is suggested that all mothers and fathers should be required to take childcare training courses. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
answer:
It is believed by some that all young first time parents should receive formal training to care 
for their child. I strongly agree that all parents should get childcare training, even if they have 
to hire professional nannies for this purpose.  
 
Childcare courses are important for many reasons. Firstly, traditional childcare skills, which 
are passed on from one generation to another, through oral and informal instruction, are not 
sufficient in today’s era of nuclear families. So parents should undergo childcare training. It is 
also a misconceived idea that childcare is a simple process of feeding children, changing 
diapers and making them sleep regularly. Contemporary childcare is not limited to this. 
Childcare is a complex science that goes beyond nutrition. It involves the physical and 
emotional wellbeing of children. Therefore, with the changing times and changing family 
structure, childcare training courses should be the norm for all would be parents.   
 
Secondly, childcare training teaches parents how to take a holistic approach to care for their 
children. Many people might wrongly think that childcare is all about love. Parents have to 
learn when to be firm, and when to give some room to children. For example, children eat a 
lot of candy, without knowledge that candy can cause obesity and tooth damage. Parents 
should not respond to children's needs for candy permanently.  
 
Furthermore, quality childcare has many other far-reaching benefits. Current research has 
shown that the early years (ages 0-5) are the most sensitive for brain development. Over 90% 
of brain growth occurs during this period. Studies show that children who get good care, enter 
school with better math, language and social skills. Finally, parents, who have themselves 
done such course, can monitor the childcare being given by a professional nanny, better.  
 
To summarise, successful childcare does not lie only in love but also in other skills. Therefore, 
all young parents join childcare training courses.

title: When families have a meal together it is considered social activity. What are the advantag…
question: When families have a meal together it is considered social activity. What are the advantages of a family meal? Do you think eating together is important to people in your country?
answer:
It is irrefutable that eating together is a social activity. There are many advantages of families 
sitting together and sharing a meal. Eating together is definitely significant to people of my 
country, India. 
 
The first and foremost advantage of eating together is that it creates a sense of belonging. 
Conversations during the meal provide opportunities for the family to bond and learn from 
one another. It is a chance to share information and news of the day, as well as give extra 
attention to your children and teens. Family meals foster warmth, security and love, as well 
as feelings of belonging. It can be a unifying experience for all.  
 
Secondly, family mealtime is the perfect opportunity to teach appropriate table manners, 
etiquette, and social skills. Parents can be perfect role models in this and children learn by 
following them. What is more, meals prepared and eaten at home are usually more nutritious 
and healthy. They contain more fruits, vegetables, and dairy products along with additional 
nutrients such as fiber, calcium, vitamins A and C, and folate.  
 
Furthermore, research shows that frequent family dinners (five or more a week), are 
associated with lower rates of smoking, drinking, and illegal drug use in pre-teens and 
teenagers when compared to families that eat together two or fewer times per week. To add 
to it, children do better in school when they eat more meals with their parents and family. 
 
In my country most people do value shared mealtime. However, the fast-paced life and 
influence of the global culture is taking some away from this custom. Fortunately, some 
recent studies have shown that even in the developed countries people are realizing the 
importance of family meals and are downshifting. It is indeed time to bring the "family" back 
to the dinner table. 
 
To conclude, eating together is definitely an important social activity. That is why it has been 
said that, ‘The family that eats together stays together’.

title: Some people say that parents have the most important role in a child’s development. Howeve…
question: Some people say that parents have the most important role in a child’s development. However, others argue that other things like television or friends have the most significant influence. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
answer:
Some individuals are of the opinion that parents have the most significant role in a child’s 
development, whereas others opine that friends and other environmental factors such as TV 
have a more important role. This essay shall discuss both perspectives. I believe that all the 
factors like parents, peers and TV, are inextricably linked and it is not possible to say which 
factor has more role.   
 
There are reasons why some people hold the opinion that parents have the most critical role 
in a child’s development. Firstly, parents have direct interaction with the children. They have 
their greatest effect on intellectual development and character traits of their children. They 
also play a very important role in the socializing process of the child. Right from the bedtime 
stories to the behavioural habits, parents play a very important role in making a child a 
responsible citizen. That is why it is believed by some that parents have the strongest role in 
a child’s development. 
 
On the other hand, those who say that friends and TV have more vital role on the 
development of children, give their reasons as follows. Firstly, children can relate better to 
their friends as they are of the same age group. They find comfort in these friendships when 
things get tough such as losing a pet or facing family problems. Television is also one of the 
most prevalent media influences in children’s lives. How much impact TV has on children 
depends on how much they watch, what they watch and with whom they watch.   
 
In my opinion, we cannot generalize as to what has more significance. In the early years family 
generally has more impact but in adolescence, peers and TV may impact more. It has also 
been seen that the power of the peer group becomes more important when the family 
relationships are not close or supportive. For example, if the parents work extra jobs and are 
largely unavailable, their children may turn to their peer group for emotional support.  
 
To sum up, behaviour is affected by a complex interaction of many different factors such as 
parents, peers and environment. It is difficult to generalize which factor plays the most 
significant role.

question: Nowadays, some buildings, such as offices and schools have open- space design instead of separate rooms. Why is it so? Do you think  it is a positive or a negative development?
answer:
Introduction 
A comfortable environment in classrooms and at the workplace is very 
essential as we spend a lot of time there. Contemporary architecture is 
promoting open layouts in such places. This essay intends to analyze 
the reasons for this. While this has a few drawbacks, the benefits are 
far more. 

Why is it so 
The most important reason for this to happen is, having specious 
open plans for schools can be cost-effective. Since the cost of land has 
increased a lot in recent years, especially in urban areas, having an 
open design is a lot cheaper. Where, on a low budget, a lot more 
students and staff can be accommodated, and at the same time 
windows and doors are not required.

One reason why this is a positive development is, openness promotes 
sharing and this in effect promotes cooperation and productivity. In 
open offices, employees have to share equipment like stationery, 
which leads to more communication. Additionally, there is better 
collaboration in open spaces. In open classrooms, children can see 
each other’s progress and help each other. For example, children who 
are strong in mathematics can help other students with difficult 
concepts like calculus, algebra etcetera. All these pros mentioned 
above explain why such architecture is becoming popular.

Conclusion

disadvantages, I still consider the growing trend of open offices and

title:
Today, many people rely on the internet to diagnose and cure their 
own health problems in…
question: Today, many people rely on the internet to diagnose and cure their  own health problems instead of seeing a doctor. Is it a positive or  negative development?
answer:
Introduction 
Nowadays people use the internet to self-diagnose their ailments 
instead of seeing a doctor. I think cost, time and convenience are the 
main reasons for this change. I believe web diagnosis can be 
inaccurate and relying on it for curing health problems is dangerous. 

Negative 
development 1

As cities become overcrowded, problems relating to housing and

advantages are far more.

beneficial for cities as well as rural areas. It can address the problems 
caused by excessive population density in cities such as high living

government of my city, Khulna, motivated all industries to shift to rural 
areas. Now my city has cleaner air and way less traffic than in the past.

costs are less in rural areas. Local people in villages are also more

a result, industries like food processing, and furniture making are now 
located in rural areas because relocating to rural areas can cut down 
several costs for businesses.

support the businesses. In other words, it might be difficult for

similar businesses in the area. For example, readymade garments

To sum up, although companies might face certain problems with

question: Many aspects of the way people dress today are influenced by global  fashion trends.  How has global fashion become such a strong influence on people’s  lives?  Do you think this is a positive or negative development?
answer:
In recent years, global fashion trends have played a major role in 
shaping the way people dress. With the rapid spread of information 
and international brands, clothing styles from one part of the world 
can quickly become popular across different cultures. While this global 
influence has brought certain benefits, it also raises some concerns. 

One major way how global fashion has become so influential is the 
growth of digital media. Social networking platforms such as 
Instagram constantly expose users to celebrities and influencers who 
promote specific styles. As people spend more time online, they are 
more likely to imitate these trends in order to feel modern and socially 
accepted. In addition, international clothing brands like Zara and 
Nike operate in almost every major city, making global fashion easily 
accessible. 

From a positive perspective, global fashion allows individuals to 
express themselves more creatively and confidently. People now have 
access to a wider variety of styles, fabrics, and designs than ever 
before. For example, a young person in a developing country can 
adopt professional Western clothing for work while still blending it with 
traditional elements. Another advantage is that the global fashion 
industry creates economic opportunities by supporting millions of jobs 
worldwide. 

However, people being influenced by international fashion trends 
has a negative effect as well. Global fashion can weaken local 
cultures, as traditional clothing may be seen as outdated by 
younger generations, leading to a gradual loss of cultural identity. 

In conclusion, global fashion has become highly influential mainly due 
to digital media and international brands. Although it offers greater 
choice and economic benefits, its cultural consequences mean that its 
influence should be approached with caution.

title:

question: Some people have decided to reduce the number of times they fly  every year or to stop flying altogether.  Do you think the environmental benefits of this development  outweigh the disadvantages for individuals and businesses?
answer:
In recent years, a growing number of people have chosen to reduce how 
often they travel by air or to stop flying altogether, mainly due to 
environmental concerns. While this trend brings clear ecological 
benefits, it also creates certain challenges for individuals and 
businesses. 

One of the major advantages of this is, flying less can 
significantly reduce carbon emissions. Air travel is one of the fastest-
growing sources of greenhouse gases, and even a small decrease in 
passenger numbers can help lower fuel consumption and air pollution. 
For example, business meetings that were previously held in 
different countries are now often conducted online, which saves 
energy and reduces the environmental impact. 

Additionally, the reduction of noise pollution around airports, which 
can improve the quality of life for nearby residents. For instance, 
during the COVID-19 pandemic, when international flights were 
sharply reduced, many people living near major airports such as 
Heathrow in London or JFK in New York reported noticeably quieter 
surroundings and better sleep. In the long term, this shift could 
contribute to slowing climate change and improving overall 
environmental conditions. 

However, reducing air travel could limit people’s ability to travel freely 
and cultural exchange, as many people depend on flights to visit family 
or study abroad. At the same time, it may harm industries such as 
tourism and aviation, particularly in countries that rely heavily on 
international visitors. For example, destinations like Thailand or Spain 
could face job losses and reduced national income if fewer foreign 
tourists are able to travel there. 

In conclusion, although reducing air travel creates challenges, the 
long-term environmental gains are more important and justify this 
development.

question: In many countries, primary and secondary schools close for two  months or more in the summer holidays.  What is the value of long school holidays? What are the  arguments in favor of shorter school holidays?
answer:
In many countries, schools close for a long period during the 
summer holidays, often for two months or more. While long breaks 
have several benefits for both students and teachers, there are also 
strong reasons to support shorter school holidays. 

One major value of long school holidays is that students can 
rest and recover from study pressure. During the school year, 
children deal with regular exams, homework, and deadlines, which 
can make them feel tired and stressed. A long break gives them 
time to relax and spend more time with their families. For example, 
many students use the summer vacation to learn new things such as 
swimming or cooking. These activities help them develop skills that 
are not taught in the classroom. In addition, teachers also benefit 
from extended holidays, as it allows them to recharge and return to 
work with renewed motivation. 

However, shorter holidays could provide more structure in 
children’s daily lives, which is particularly important for younger 
students who need routine and continuous academic progress. To 
exemplify, a six-year-old may lose their daily routine during long 
holidays, sleeping late and spending most of the day on a mobile 
phone. Shorter breaks help them return to school before these 
inappropriate habits develop. Besides, Teachers can see regular 
improvement among students when learning is not interrupted for 
too long. This is especially helpful for weaker students who struggle 
to catch up after long gaps. 

In conclusion, although long summer holidays allow students and 
teachers to rest and grow beyond the classroom, shorter holidays 
may lead to better academic consistency and reduce difficulties for 
both.

title: Bar chart
question:
The chart shows the percentages of the population living in urban areas in the world and in different regions.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
answer:
The bar chart shows the amount of people living in cities around the world and in six different regions in 1975, 2020, and a projection for 2050. Overall, the number of people living in urban areas has been growing steadily, although the rate of change is different in each region.

Between 1975 and 2020, the world’s urban population increased from less than 40% to nearly 56%, and it is expected to go over two-thirds by 2050. Asia and Africa had the lowest urban populations in 1975, both around 25%. By 2020, Asia had reached 50%, and Africa near about 43%, with both regions expected to grow by about 15% more by 2050. However, these regions are still projected to remain the least urbanized.

On the other hand, North America, Europe, and Latin America have always had more people living in cities than Asia and Africa. North America started its population range at about 73% in 1975 and is predicted to reach almost 90% by 2050 while Latin America is expected to grow nearly 25% in this period. Europe also showed a steady increase. Oceania has stayed mostly the same, with a small drop in 2020 and a slight increase again by 2050, remaining around 70%.

title: Pie charts
question:
The charts below show the average consumption of three nutrients by adults in the UK which are grown by them and may be unhealthy if eaten too much.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
answer:
The three pie charts illustrate the proportion of sodium, saturated fat, and added sugar consumed daily by adults in the UK, categorized by meals such as breakfast, lunch, dinner, and snacks. Overall, dinner accounts for the highest intake of sodium and saturated fat, while added sugar is primarily consumed through snacks. Breakfast consistently contributes the least across all three nutrients, many of which are likely selected or prepared by individuals themselves and could pose health risks if consumed in excess.

Sodium and saturated fat follow a comparable pattern across meals, with dinner contributing the highest amounts—42% for sodium and 39% for saturated fat. Lunch is the second-largest source, making up 28% and 26% respectively. In contrast, breakfast and snacks account for smaller proportions: 13% and 17% for sodium, and 16% and 19% for saturated fat.

Added sugar, on the other hand, shows a distinctly different trend. The highest intake occurs during snack times, which make up a significant 45% of the total. Meanwhile, breakfast, lunch, and dinner each contribute relatively smaller and fairly similar percentages, ranging between 16% and 20%.

title: Line graph
question:
The graph below gives information about the percentage of the population in four countries living in cities from 1970 to 2020, with predictions for 2030 and 2040.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
answer:
The line graph shows the percentage of people living in cities in four Asian countries from 1970 to 2020, with predictions for 2030 to 2040. Overall, Malaysia had the largest share of city residents, while Thailand had the smallest. Philippines and Indonesia had shown quite similar growth.

To begin with, about 30% of Malaysia’s population lived in cities in 1970. This number grew a lot and reached almost 80% by 2020. It is expected to rise further to nearly 90% by 2040. On the other hand, only 19% of people in Thailand lived in cities in 1970. This figure went up slowly to about 30% by 2020 and is likely to increase more in the future.

In the Philippines, the city population grew nearly 20% more from 1970 to 1990. Then, it dropped slightly to around 45% in 2020, but it is expected to go back up to 50% by 2040. Indonesia had the lowest urban population in 1970 at 13%, but it rose quickly to about 50% by 2020 and is expected to reach up to 63% by 2040.

title: Table
question:
The tables below give information about the world population and distribution in 1950 and 2000, with an estimate of the situation in 2050.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
answer:
The table displays the global population distribution across different continents in 1950 and 2000, along with projections for 2050. Overall, Asia consistently holds the largest share of the population, while Africa is expected to see significant growth, and Europe and North America are projected to decline further.

Between 1950 and 2000, three continents experienced an increase in their population share: Asia, Africa, and South America. Africa accounted for 9% of the global population in 1950 and rose steadily to 13%, with a further 7% increase projected by 2050. Similarly, Latin America saw modest growth during this period, and is expected to expand by additional 3% by 2050. Though Asia went through and increase from 1950 to 2000, it won’t follow the same growth as predicted. Oceania maintained a consistently small share across all periods.

In contrast, Europe and North America saw declines in their population proportions. Europe dropped significantly from 22% to 12% in 2000 and is anticipated to decrease further to 7% by 2050. North America, starting at 7% in 1950, experienced a slight dip by 2000 and is expected to fall a bit more. Regarding total global population, a dramatic rise is projected, reaching 9 billion in 2050—increasing nearly 4 times more compared to 1950.

title: Mixed graph
question:
The charts below give information on the location and the types of dance classes young people in a town in Australia are currently attending.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
answer:
The charts illustrate the percentage of different venues used for dance classes and the number of students attending various dance styles in a town in Australia. Overall, private studios are the most commonly used locations for dance lessons, while ballet is particularly popular among younger children.

Private studios account for the largest share of dance class venues, comprising nearly 50% of the total. School halls used after school hours are the second most common, representing 24%, followed by community halls at 18%. In contrast, college studios are the least frequently used, making up only 10% of the locations.

Regarding dance styles, preferences differ between age groups. Among students aged 11 to 16, modern dance is the most popular, attracting over 500 participants. Tap dance follows closely, with more than 400 students, whereas ballet is slightly less preferred in this age group. Conversely, students under the age of 11 show a strong interest in ballet, with participation reaching 600—the highest figure across all categories. Tap and modern dance are less popular among younger students, with just over 400 and 300 participants, respectively.

title: Map
question:
The maps below show a harbour in 2000 and how it looks today.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
answer:
The maps depict the layout of Porth Harbor in the past and after recent developments. Overall, the area has been transformed from a mainly commercial and private boating zone into a more recreational space, with upgraded facilities and expanded services.

Previously, the harbor had a single dock in the north, situated by the side of a public beach that still exists today. A new dock has now been added there to serve passenger ferries. The marina for private yachts, which was located near showers, toilets, and a car park connected to the main road, has been relocated further south while switching its position with the area of fishing boats.

In the southwest part, the new marina is now situated beside the newly built facilities of showers and toilets and an existing second car park. On the eastern side, while the lifeboat station remains, several new features—including shops, cafes, and a hotel—have been added, with access provided by a new road. The public beach has become a private property now.

title: Process diagram
question:
The diagram below shows how fabric is manufactured from bamboo.

Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.
answer:
The diagram illustrates the process of producing fabric from bamboo. It is apparent that, the procedure consists of nine stages starting from the cultivation and harvesting of bamboo to the production of finished garments through some mechanical and chemical processing. The process involves both natural and man-made steps.

In the first stage, bamboo is planted in the spring and harvested by hand in the autumn. After harvesting, the bamboo stalks are cut into strips using a circular saw. These strips are then crushed to produce a liquid pulp, completing the mechanical processing phase.

The next stage starts with chemical processing where the liquid pulp is filtered to separate the longer fibers. After that, water and amine oxide are added to soften the fibers. These softened fibers are then spun into threads, which are woven into fabric. In the final step, the fabric is used to make clothing products ready for sale.

title: Adding Information — Transitions
question:
Transitions:
In addition / Additionally / Furthermore / Moreover / Plus / ...as well

"Transitions" are words that help connect ideas in a paragraph.
When you are giving many examples or ideas in the body of a paragraph, you should try to introduce each idea with a transition word. (You should not start a sentence with "And".) There are many transitions that mean "Also" or "And":

In addition / Additionally / Furthermore / Moreover / Plus / ...as well

These transitions are similar to "Also". They are explained in detail below.

1. In addition / Additionally

In addition and Additionally are used to give more information about something. When you write a formal essay, you should not start a sentence with the word "And". You can often use "In addition" or "Additionally" instead of "And".
• I studied journalism in college. In addition, I had a part-time job at a newspaper.
• I joined the guitar club and the math club in school. Additionally, I went on a camping trip with the debate team.

2. Furthermore / Moreover

Furthermore and Moreover are also very formal, and they are basically the same as "in addition" and "additionally". We often use "moreover" and "furthermore" when we talk about our opinions.
• Smoking is a bad habit because it smells bad and it can damage your health. Furthermore, it is a very expensive habit.
• The politician is too old to be our president. Moreover, he is not trustworthy.
• Students are given too many tests these days. Moreover, they don't have enough free time.
• Human beings must take care of their environment. We should drive more fuel-efficient cars, and we should recycle. Furthermore, we should stop businesses from polluting the environment.

3. Plus / ...as well

Plus and ...as well can be formal or informal. ("...as well" is used at the end of a sentence.)
• That car has new brakes, an air-conditioner, and a new CD player. Plus, it has an alarm.
• The typhoon destroyed my cousin's home, and it destroyed his car as well.
• My grandfather fought in two wars, and he travelled around the world. He ran his own business as well.
• That computer is way too expensive. Plus, it's not even that good.

Note: If the sentence is negative, use either instead of as well.
• I like math, and I like science as well.
• I don't like math, and I don't like science either.

title: Contrast — Transitions
question:
However / Nevertheless / Still / Despite that / Nonetheless / Even so

When you write a formal essay, you should not start a sentence with "And", "But", or "So". In this section, you will learn some transition words that you can use instead of "And", "But", or "So".

These transitions can all be used instead of "And" (these were introduced on the previous pages):
In addition / Additionally / Furthermore / Moreover / Plus

Note: You usually start a new sentence with these transitions. You can also put these after a semi-colon (;).
Note: When you start a sentence with these words, you need to put a comma after them.

Additionally, you can use the following transitions instead of "But":
However / Nevertheless / Still / Despite that / Nonetheless / Even so

Examples:
• I'm a vegetarian. However, I sometimes eat fish.
• Tom said his English is terrible. Nevertheless, he got a perfect score on his English test.
• Pakistan is a dangerous country for travelers. Still, I want to go explore it someday.
• The water in the city is not safe to drink. Despite that, Kim gives it to her dog to drink.
• Terry is afraid to speak in front of people. Nonetheless, she is giving a speech at the United Nations next week.
• Brian goes to church every Sunday. Even so, he can be very rude.
• The tornado destroyed the entire town. However, no one was killed.
• The doctor said that Benjamin needs to stop eating meat. Nevertheless, he still eats a hamburger every day for lunch.
• Joseph said that his father is rich. Still, he should get a job and learn to be responsible with money.
• The school said that we can't wear shorts. Despite that, Julie wore her new shorts and was told to go home.
• It has been raining for a week. Nonetheless, we're going to try to go camping this weekend.
• Our guitarist is sick. Even so, we're going to perform without him tonight.

title: Punctuation — Rules and Practice
question:
When you use transitions, you have to be careful with punctuation.
For example, with these transitions, you need to know the three rules below:

However / Nevertheless / Still / Despite that / Nonetheless / Even so
Therefore / Consequently / As a Result / Thus / For this reason

1. You need to put a comma after them when they are at the beginning of a sentence.
→ My father is very strict. However, I know that he loves me.
→ Tennis is a very fun sport. Therefore, I play every weekend.

2. Also, you can use a semi-colon (...; however,...) or a period (... . However,...).
→ We studied very hard; despite that, we both failed the test.
→ We studied very hard. Despite that, we both failed the test.

3. You can not use only a comma (..., however,...).
→ James lost his job, consequently, he had to move in with his parents. (Wrong!)
→ James lost his job. Consequently, he had to move in with his parents. (Right!)
→ James lost his job; consequently, he had to move in with his parents. (Right!)

Write "C" if the punctuation is "correct" or "I" if the punctuation is incorrect.
If you write "I", fix the punctuation. (See page 77 for sample answers.)

4. The politician has lied to the people many times. Still, many people vote for him.
5. Our team trained much harder than the other teams, as a result we won the championship.
6. This computer is the most expensive one; however, I don't think it's the best.
7. Jack didn't have health insurance, consequently, he couldn't get treatment when he got sick.

title: Community and change · Task 1
question:
The table shows the percentages of commuters using buses and bicycles in fictional City 1 in three years. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Year | Bus | Bicycle
2010 | 30 | 10
2015 | 45 | 20
2020 | 50 | 35
answer:
The table compares the proportions of commuters travelling by bus and bicycle in a fictional city in 2010, 2015 and 2020. Overall, both forms of transport became more common, but buses remained the more widely used option throughout the period. The increase in cycling was larger in percentage-point terms.

In 2010, buses accounted for 30% of commuters, compared with 10% for bicycles. By 2015, the bus figure had risen to 45%, while cycling reached 20%. This left a gap of 25 percentage points between the two modes in the middle year.

By 2020, the share using buses stood at 50%, representing an overall rise of 20 percentage points. Bicycle use reached 35%, an increase of 25 points from its initial level. Consequently, the difference between the two modes narrowed from 20 points in 2010 to 15 points in 2020. These figures describe separate proportions and do not imply that the categories represent all commuting methods.
grammar: Introduce the measures and years. Give an overview of both trends. Compare the beginning and end, then support comparisons with figures.

title: Community and change · Task 2
question: Cities should invest more in public libraries than in entertainment facilities. To what extent do you agree or disagree?
answer:
Public libraries deserve substantial investment because they support education and provide access to services that many residents cannot obtain privately. However, I do not think that cities should neglect entertainment entirely. A sensible policy gives libraries reliable funding while assessing other facilities according to their public value.

One reason to prioritise libraries is that their benefits reach beyond borrowing books. Students can use quiet study areas, job seekers can access information, and residents can attend affordable learning activities. For example, a library that lends equipment and teaches basic repair skills can reduce the cost of learning a practical activity. These services are especially valuable to people whose homes lack space or resources. Investment should therefore include trained staff as well as buildings.

Nevertheless, entertainment facilities can also serve the community. A public theatre or sports centre may provide opportunities for social contact, exercise and cultural participation. The question is whether the facility is accessible and whether its benefits justify the cost. A very expensive venue used by a small group should not automatically receive priority over a widely used library. Conversely, a modest recreation space in an underserved neighbourhood may be an excellent investment.

Cities should therefore compare needs rather than treat every library as beneficial and every entertainment project as unnecessary. They can examine likely users, operating costs and barriers to access before allocating funds. Public consultation can reveal needs that a simple attendance forecast misses. In my view, libraries should receive a strong funding foundation, but the remaining budget should support a balanced range of services that residents can realistically use.
grammar: Define your position and two main reasons. Plan one claim, explanation and example per body paragraph. Address the exact task and conclude without a new argument.

The chart and table show the numbers of books borrowed from a fictional college library in three categories in 2015 and 2025. Summarise the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

Category | 2015 | 2025
Science | 120 | 180
History | 100 | 90
Literature | 80 | 150
answer:
The chart compares the numbers of science, history and literature books borrowed from a fictional college library in 2015 and 2025. Overall, borrowing increased in science and literature, while history was the only category to decline. Science remained the most frequently borrowed category in both years.

In 2015, 120 science books were borrowed, compared with 100 history books and 80 literature books. Thus, the difference between the highest and lowest categories was 40 books. Ten years later, science borrowing reached 180, representing an increase of 60 books. Literature rose more sharply, from 80 to 150, a gain of 70 books.

By contrast, the number of history books borrowed fell from 100 to 90. This placed history below literature in 2025, whereas their order had been reversed in 2015. Total borrowing across the three categories increased from 300 to 420 books. The figures therefore show both an overall rise in borrowing and a change in the relative popularity of the subjects. They do not provide information about the reasons for these changes.

title: Evidence and learning · Task 2
question: Some people think students should study alone, while others favour collaborative learning. Discuss both views and give your opinion.
answer:
Studying alone and learning with others offer different advantages. Independent study can improve concentration, while collaboration can reveal misunderstandings and encourage learners to explain their ideas. I believe that students benefit most from combining the two, with the balance determined by the task.

Those who favour studying alone often value control over time and pace. A learner can spend longer on a difficult passage without waiting for a group or feeling embarrassed. Independent retrieval practice also shows what the student can remember without assistance. For instance, closing a textbook and writing a short explanation can expose gaps that would be hidden if another person supplied the answer. A quiet environment is therefore useful for both concentration and honest self-assessment.

Collaborative learning provides a different kind of feedback. Students must express their understanding clearly, and a partner may question an assumption that initially seemed obvious. Comparing two explanations of the same sentence can reveal an important difference in meaning. However, group work is less useful if one participant completes the task while the others remain passive. Teachers should assign roles and ensure that everyone contributes rather than assume that sitting together produces learning.

In my view, students should first make an individual attempt and then discuss selected problems. They can return to independent work afterwards to check whether they can apply the explanation themselves. This sequence preserves personal responsibility while taking advantage of other perspectives. It also avoids making collaboration a substitute for effort. Ultimately, neither method is universally superior: effective study requires choosing an approach that supports the intended learning outcome and checking whether understanding has actually improved.

title: Systems and communication · Task 2
question: Many cities experience traffic congestion. What are the main causes, and what measures could address this problem?
answer:
Traffic congestion results from several connected pressures, including concentrated travel demand and limited alternatives to private vehicles. Although building roads may help in specific locations, a lasting response should also make other forms of transport practical and reduce unnecessary peak-hour journeys.

A major cause is that many people travel to the same destinations at similar times. Schools and workplaces often begin together, producing demand that exceeds available road capacity. In addition, residents may choose cars because buses are unreliable or walking routes feel unsafe. In these circumstances, asking people to change their habits without improving their options is unlikely to work. A commuter who cannot depend on a bus arriving on time has a strong reason to continue driving.

One solution is to improve the reliability of public transport. Dedicated bus lanes, clear service information and convenient connections can make a journey more predictable. Cities can also create safer walking and cycling routes for shorter trips. These improvements should connect homes with actual destinations rather than form isolated sections. Meanwhile, employers can offer flexible starting times where the nature of the work allows it, spreading demand over a longer period.

Policies should be evaluated carefully. A road project may remove a bottleneck, but its cost and effects on neighbouring streets should be considered. Likewise, a new bus route is not successful merely because it exists; frequency and accessibility matter. In my view, cities should combine targeted infrastructure improvements with dependable alternatives and flexible travel arrangements. This approach addresses the reasons people drive while recognising that some journeys will still require private vehicles.
